title: twostep: E2SFCA Accessibility to OB/GYN Subspecialists in the Contiguous United States
description:
Standalone analysis and manuscript for national travel-time accessibility to the seven ABOG-certified obstetric and gynecologic subspecialties across the contiguous United States, 2013-2023, using an Enhanced Two-Step Floating Catchment Area (E2SFCA) method on road-network isochrones with a mass-conserving demand allocation and a Spatial Access Ratio (SPAR).

Scientific verification. The accessibility engine is validated against published fixtures from Luo & Qi (2009) and Delamater (2013), cross-checked against two independent reference implementations, exercised by a named mutation corpus, and gated by a scientific join doctrine that fails closed on unmatched keys, duplicate keys and missing population rather than silently dropping, multiplying or zeroing them. A prespecified, hash-frozen specification-curve (multiverse) analysis reports which conclusions survive defensible alternative modelling choices.

Reproducibility. The manuscript renders from a frozen run whose inputs are verified by checksum before use, and verbal quantifiers in the paper are asserted against the values they describe at render time.

notes: Archived from the mufflyt/twostep repository. The methodological sources listed under related_identifiers are the papers this implementation reproduces and is tested against, not merely background reading: Luo & Qi (2009) supplies the E2SFCA weight sets and a published worked fixture, Delamater (2013) the M2SFCA formulation, McGrail (2012) the Gaussian decay variant, Luo & Wang (2003) the original 2SFCA baseline, and Wan et al. (2012) the Spatial Access Ratio.
